abstracts.cdata!:
Ratings for the Tamil Nadu Sustainable
            Urban Development Program Project for India were as follows:
            outcome and Bank performance was satisfactory and monitoring
            and evaluation (M and E) quality was substantial. Some
            lessons learned included: political commitment, policy
            reform, and provision of incentives are important
            ingredients for improving the financial sustainability of
            water services. Information, education, and communication
            activities are essential to instill behavioral changes and
            sustain service provision at the desired levels. The
            municipal development fund model proved to be effective in
            mobilizing much-needed urban financing and can be further
            leveraged to access the private market. Result-based
            performance grants should be scaled up to promote urban
            governance reform in urban local body (ULBs). Institutional
            strengthening and capacity building of ULBs require
            sustained support.

abstracts.cdata!:
The objective of the Tamil Nadu
            Sustainable Urban Development Project for India is to
            demonstrate improved urban management practices and improve
            urban services delivery in participating Urban Local Bodies
            (ULBs) in a financially sustainable manner. Some of the
            negative impacts and mitigation measures include: (i) all
            clearance required during construction will be ensured and
            made available before start of work; (ii) adequate measures
            will be taken and checked to control the Baseline parameters
            of Air, Water and Noise pollution; (iii) the contractor will
            identify site for temporary use of land for construction
            sites or storage of construction materials, etc.; (iv) where
            loose soil is met with, shoring and strutting will be
            provided to avoid collapse of soil; (v) a suitable site
            identified for safe disposal, in low lying areas within the
            project area as approved by the Engineer in charge and to
            other low lying area in consultation with local body; (vi)
            site identified for safe storage and handling of chemicals
            and other hazardous materials provided with proper display
            of requirements and marking as protected area; (vii) the
            contractor will provide garbage bins in the camps and ensure
            that these are regularly emptied and disposed off in a
            hygienic manner as per the Comprehensive Solid Waste
            Management Plan approved by the Engineer; (viii) maintenance
            of vehicles, equipment and machinery will be regular and up
            to the satisfaction of the Engineer to keep noise levels at
            the minimum; (ix) Control valves would be provided in the
            inlet of all booster stations, ULB sumps and service
            reservoirs to control the flow; and (x) the backwash water
            is collected in the recycle sump and the solids allowed
            settling during one hour detention period and will be
            recirculated into the treatment unit, besides this will also
            be reused for green belt.

abstracts.cdata!:
The objective of the Tamil Nadu
            Sustainable Urban Development Project for India is to
            demonstrate improved urban management practices and improve
            urban services delivery in participating Urban Local Bodies
            (ULBs) in a financially sustainable manner. Some of the
            negative impacts and mitigation measures include: (i) the
            construction work shall be done without affecting the
            existing road; (ii) the site is adjacent to Noon meal center
            of Municipal school and the construction of service
            reservoir shall not disturb the function of Noon meal
            center; (iii) there is a taxi stand adjacent to the existing
            reservoir and the proposed sump which is going to be
            constructed near the taxi stand shall not disturb any
            activities in that area; (iv) the construction of proposed
            reservoir shall not disturb social activities and the inlet
            and outlet of any water body exist in that area; (v) the
            water supply to each house will be provided with water meter
            and water tax will be collected based on the consumption of
            water; (vi) separate electrical feeder main as well as
            Diesel generators for all the pumping stations are proposed
            in this project; (vii) the distribution system for each of
            the ten Zones has been designed for equitable water supply;
            and (viii) distribution pipes will be laid at a depth
            varying from 1.05 meters to 1.55 meters below ground level.

abstracts.cdata!:
The development objective of the Tamil
            Nadu Sustainable Urban Development Project for India is to
            improve urban services delivery in participating urban local
            bodies (ULBs) in a financially sustainable manner and to
            pilot improved urban management practices in selected
            cities. Some of the negative impacts and mitigation measures
            include: (1) all cash allowances shall be revised at the
            rate of 5 percent per annum starting from the financial year
            2016-17, the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has to extend
            the R&R entitlements with revised rates (with 5 percent
            per annum) R&R assistance as it has been not revised for
            last 2 years; and (2) the structure cost for partially
            impacted structures will be paid to the structure owner
            (squatter) and wherever the tenant occupied structure or
            portion of the structure is affected, the structure cost of
            the same will be paid to the structure-owner.
